start.label: Getting Started
start.heading: What is HYDRA-UMC STUDIO?
paragraphs: HYDRA-UMC STUDIO is a centralized control dashboard for robots, CNC machines, laser engravers, 3D-printer beds, and pick-and-place stations. One dashboard, several machines, all synchronized in real time.

Start by adding a Controller (top-right selector, or Config > Controllers) - each controller represents one physical HYDRA-UMC board, reachable over Ethernet/IP. Press "Add Node" and enter its name and IP address.
Once a controller is selected, its robots are listed in the sidebar. Click a robot to open its full control panel: jog sliders, examples, recorded trajectories, and its own live 3D view.

Everything you configure - robot names, custom models, saved trajectories, tool assignments - is saved automatically to the server's data/ directory, so it survives restarts and is shared by every browser that opens the dashboard.

robots.label: Robots
robots.heading: Jogging, homing, and real kinematics
paragraphs: Each robot panel shows a live 3D view plus one rotary knob and slider per joint (J1-J6). Drag either one to jog that joint; the 3D view updates immediately.

Parol6, Faze4, AR3, and AR4 are modeled with their real mesh geometry and their manufacturer's own joint chain - jogging them moves the same way the real arm would, respecting their real joint limits where the robot defines any. The Generic model uses a simplified two-link arm with no fixed joint limits.

HOME sends the robot to a safe, reachable reference pose. STOP (top bar, Ctrl+Shift+Space) immediately halts every robot, with no confirmation. If the robot has an XY table attached, its own TX/TY jog controls appear alongside the joint sliders, and HOME XY resets just the table.
The Tool selector assigns a URTC tool (soldering iron, dispenser, screwdriver, gripper, etc.) to the robot's end effector, shown on the 3D model's tool tip.
"Combine with Robot" lets you display a second robot inside the same 3D view (for choreographed multi-robot cells) - its own motion is still configured from its own panel.

trajectories.label: Trajectories
trajectories.heading: Examples, recorded points, and playback
paragraphs: The Points Table at the bottom of a robot panel is a sequence of steps the robot moves through. Build it three ways: load a canned Example (circles, spirals, waves, pick-and-place, XY-table patterns...), jog the robot by hand and press "+ Add Point" to capture the current pose, or load a previously saved Work file.
Works are your own saved trajectories: JSON files stored per-robot on the server. Save the current Points Table with the Save button, or load/upload one from the Works Robot selector.
Every step can be reordered (up/down arrows), edited (pencil icon - joint angles, and XY-table position if applicable), or deleted (trash icon) directly in the table.

Use Play/Pause/Stop to run the sequence, Repeat to loop it, and the Speed slider to scale playback speed. The cyan line drawn in the 3D view previews the tool tip's Cartesian path for the loaded steps before you even press Play.

Steps loaded from an Example are portable between robot models: the app converts each step to a real-world Cartesian target and re-solves it for whichever robot is currently selected, so the same example traces a sensible path on a Parol6, an AR4, or the Generic arm alike.

modules.label: Modules
modules.heading: Machines beyond robot arms
paragraphs: XY Table: configure a motorized XY platform's size and jog it independently, or attach it under a robot for pick-and-place work.
ATC Tools: define tool-changer slots and their offsets so a robot can pick up and swap between physical tools automatically.
Rack Manager: organize storage racks/bins used by pick-and-place routines.
Pick & Place, CNC, and Laser: each gets its own dedicated control panel (position jog, speed, active tool/job) once enabled for a robot.
Vacuum Table: control pump and valve state and monitor pressure for vacuum hold-down work.
Heated Bed: set a target temperature and monitor the actual bed temperature for 3D-printing-style workflows.
Any module shows "Not Assigned" until you enable it for a robot from that robot's Model & Tools settings.

cameras_gamepad.label: Cameras & Gamepad
cameras_gamepad.heading: Vision and manual control
paragraphs: The Vision / Cameras view (Octal Vision Matrix) shows up to eight live feeds side by side: standard USB vision cameras or thermal cameras (MLX90640/90641/90642), with recording and live inference status.
A USB or Bluetooth gamepad can be mapped to jog robots and trigger actions manually - configure the button/axis mapping under Config > Gamepad.

firmware_settings.label: Firmware & Settings
firmware_settings.heading: Flashing boards and configuring the dashboard
paragraphs: Flasher and Tester (Shared Resources > URTC) reach a robot's own Controller Board, and its URTC Tool Head beyond it, over CAN-OTA only - no JTAG/SWD probe, no USB-CAN dongle. Flasher uploads a .bin firmware image and runs the same page-by-page transfer, CRC32/HMAC verify, and anti-rollback checks the URTC bootloader already implements; Tester queries live version info, F-RAM state, and per-tool telemetry, plus a safe self-test that never actuates at meaningful power.

Config (top bar) opens System Configuration: manage Controllers (name, IP, add/auto-search), UI & Themes (theme, language - this Help menu follows the same language), Robot Names and Custom Models, Software Integrations, Work Paths (where each robot's Works are stored), and Gamepad mapping.

Config > CAN-OTA lets you pick the transport (a full built-in simulation, or real hardware), record the Robot Controller Board's own MCU once it's confirmed, and set the firmware-file paths Flasher looks in. While the transport is the simulated one, Flasher shows a SIMULATION banner, sends nothing to the boards and never changes the saved version.
Factory Reset, inside Config, wipes all saved configuration back to defaults - use with care, it cannot be undone.

accounts_access.label: Accounts & Access
accounts_access.heading: Logging in, user accounts, and remote access
paragraphs: Every server seeds one account on its own first-ever start. On a development install it is admin / admin; in production the first administrator comes from the deployment's bootstrap settings (see the production bootstrap guide) and the server refuses example values. Change that password as soon as you can from Config > Users - otherwise anyone on the network who knows it can sign in with full access.

Config > Users lets an Administrator account create additional accounts with the Operator role: an Operator can sign in, view live state, and send robot commands (jog/play/pause/stop/tool/valve/pump/speed), but can't change global settings or manage other accounts. Use it to hand a coworker robot control without also handing them the keys to the whole configuration.

You don't have to sign in at all to look around - "Continue read-only" on the login screen lets you browse every panel and the live 3D view, you just can't save changes or send commands from that session.

Config > Remote Access has one switch per remote client - HYDRA-UMC SUITE, the Android control app, and the iOS control app - so you can allow one and block another independently. Turning one off only stops that app's own "find my server" scan from seeing this one; it doesn't password-protect the API by itself, since anyone who already has this server's IP address can still reach it directly.

ecosystem.label: Ecosystem
ecosystem.heading: STUDIO as the whole ecosystem's frontend
paragraphs: The HYDRA-UMC menu (left sidebar) is not only about this deployment's own robots - it also surfaces the whole HYDRA-UMC-* ecosystem this Server can see: which sibling projects exist, whether their own service is actually reachable, who's connected, and what the Server itself is doing.

HYDRA-UMC > Services lists every sibling HYDRA-UMC-* project checked out next to this Server, with a real live probe (TCP/HTTP) for whichever ones declare their own port - a green or red dot, not just a maturity label. There's no start/stop here yet: no process supervisor exists anywhere in the ecosystem today.

HYDRA-UMC > Telemetry runs real raw or aggregated queries against HYDRA-UMC-DATALAKE's own stored readings. HYDRA-UMC > AI Family narrows that same Services scan to the Vision AI (Hailo-8, today's camera/detection pipeline) and Cognitive AI (Hailo-10 8GB, planned) nodes - see Config > AI/Hailo to record which chip is actually installed on this deployment and where compiled models live.

Connected Apps, Server Logs and Server Admin (HYDRA-UMC menu, admin accounts only) mirror the same admin API this Server's own reference admin panel uses: every live connection right now, a tail of the Server's own log file, and its listen port plus a graceful restart.

ecosystem.plan_duration_hint: Durations: 90s, 1m, 1h, 30d, 2w, 5y or milliseconds. Leave the optional cells empty. Kind * and field * is the default tier.
ecosystem.plan_delete_label: Delete the raw points that were rolled up
ecosystem.plan_delete_disabled: Disabled: the operator has to start the data lake with --downsample-allow-delete. No request can switch it on.
ecosystem.plan_delete_warning: Rolled-up raw points are removed for good, and the rollups past their retention are removed too. Read the effects before saving.
ecosystem.plan_mode_dryrun: Mode now: dry run (reports, deletes nothing)
ecosystem.plan_strict_note: Strict rules, always on: the rollup width is not longer than the raw time, no retention is shorter than the raw time, the narrow retention is not longer than the rollup retention, the narrow width divides the rollup width, no tier is listed twice and every kind exists in the data lake. The data lake has no option to relax them.
ecosystem.plan_invalid_count: {{count}} problem(s): the plan cannot be saved.
ecosystem.plan_saved: Plan saved. The timer uses it from its next round.
ecosystem.plan_unchanged: Nothing changed: the data lake already has this plan.
ecosystem.plan_confirm_message: The data lake will use this plan from its next round. A saved plan never runs by itself.
ecosystem.plan_confirm_delete_message: This turns real deletion ON: the raw points that were rolled up will be removed for good. Are you sure?
ecosystem.plan_effects: Effects of the next round: {{raw}} raw point(s) to roll up, {{rollups}} rollup(s) and {{fine}} narrow rollup(s) to expire.
ecosystem.plan_previewed: Checked with the data lake: the plan is accepted.
ecosystem.plan_error_plan_changed: The plan changed since you read it. Read it again before saving.
ecosystem.plan_error_confirm_delete_required: Turning deletion on needs your explicit confirmation after reading the effects.
ecosystem.plan_error_delete_not_allowed: The data lake was not started with --downsample-allow-delete, so a plan that deletes is refused.
ecosystem.plan_error_invalid_plan: The data lake rejected the shape of the plan.
ecosystem.plan_error_incoherent_plan: The widths or retentions of the plan do not fit together.
ecosystem.plan_error_unknown_kind: The plan names a kind this data lake does not know.
ecosystem.plan_error_invalid_request: The data lake did not understand the request.
ecosystem.plan_error_write_failed: The data lake could not write the plan; the old plan is untouched.
ecosystem.plan_issue_default_needs_star_field: A field needs a kind: only the default tier is * and *.
ecosystem.plan_issue_bad_duration: {{value}} is not a duration such as 90s, 1h, 30d or 5y.
ecosystem.plan_issue_fine_not_smaller: The narrow width must be smaller than the rollup width.
ecosystem.plan_issue_fine_not_divisor: The narrow width must divide the rollup width exactly.
ecosystem.plan_issue_fine_too_many: At most {{max}} narrow buckets per rollup bucket.
ecosystem.plan_issue_fine_retention_needs_fine: The narrow retention needs a narrow width.
ecosystem.plan_issue_fine_retention_on_default: The narrow retention is not available on the default tier.
ecosystem.plan_issue_fine_retention_longer: The narrow retention must not be longer than the rollup retention.
ecosystem.plan_issue_bucket_longer_than_raw: The rollup width must not be longer than the raw time.
ecosystem.plan_issue_rollup_shorter_than_raw: The rollup retention must not be shorter than the raw time.
ecosystem.plan_issue_fine_retention_shorter_than_r: The narrow retention must not be shorter than the raw time.
ecosystem.plan_issue_unknown_kind: The kind {{kind}} has no data and no policy in this data lake.
ecosystem.clients_desc: Every live connection to this Server right now (STUDIO tabs, mobile apps, HYDRA-UMC SUITE, ...) - not the robot roster itself.
ecosystem.logs_footer_live: Last {{lines}} lines of this Server's own log file, refreshing every {{seconds}}s.
ecosystem.logs_footer_paused: Last {{lines}} lines of this Server's own log file (paused).
ecosystem.logs_load_error: Could not load the server log.
ecosystem.admin_server_port_note: Saving does NOT change the running server - this process cannot rebind its own listening socket without dropping every open connection. It takes effect on the next restart.
ecosystem.admin_server_restart_confirm: Restart this Server now? Every connected device will briefly disconnect and reconnect. Only actually restarts if this process runs under a supervisor (systemd/pm2/Docker) configured to auto-restart on exit.
ecosystem.admin_server_port_invalid: Port must be a number between 1 and 65535.
ecosystem.admin_server_port_saved: Port saved - restart this server for it to take effect.
ecosystem.admin_server_load_error: Could not reach the server admin API.
ecosystem.admin_security_info_label: Ask for sign-in on the host information (metrics, process supervisor, ecosystem status)
ecosystem.admin_security_info_off_confirm: Turn the sign-in requirement off? The host information (metrics, process supervisor, ecosystem status) will be readable by anyone on the network.
ecosystem.admin_security_info_off_warning: The host information is now readable by the whole network.
ecosystem.admin_security_tls_paths_required: To turn TLS on, give the path of the certificate and of the key.
ecosystem.admin_security_tls_inactive: The running server does not use TLS.
ecosystem.admin_security_tls_restart: The change applies on the next restart.
ecosystem.admin_security_source_env: Set in the environment of the server (locked)
ecosystem.admin_security_ble_commands: Phones read the state and send commands
ecosystem.admin_security_ble_encryption: Ask for an encrypted Bluetooth link
ecosystem.admin_security_ble_unencrypted_confirm: Allow commands over Bluetooth without an encrypted link? The access token of the account travels in every command, so anyone near the server could read it.
ecosystem.admin_security_ble_unencrypted_warning: Commands over Bluetooth are allowed without an encrypted link: anyone near the server could read the access tokens.
ecosystem.admin_security_mqtt_state: Publish the state of the robots
ecosystem.admin_security_mqtt_commands: Publish the state and carry out commands
ecosystem.admin_security_mqtt_command_user: Account that carries the commands out
ecosystem.admin_security_mqtt_passwords: The passwords are set in the environment of the server, never here.
ecosystem.admin_security_mqtt_commands_confirm: Carry out commands that arrive on the MQTT broker? Each runs with the role of the account named here, through the same rules as any client.
ecosystem.admin_security_mqtt_commands_warning: Commands over MQTT are on: whoever can publish on the broker can drive the robots within the role of that account.
ecosystem.admin_security_mqtt_invalid: Check the MQTT fields: the address starts with mqtt://, mqtts://, ws:// or wss://, and commands need the account that carries them out.
ecosystem.admin_security_voice_heard_label: A voice reply repeats what was said (personal data; off by default)
ecosystem.admin_security_voice_confidence_label: Least confidence of the speech recognizer (0 to 1) to accept a request that starts a movement
ecosystem.admin_security_voice_help: Applies from the next voice turn. 0 switches the confidence check off; a stop is never held back. The environment of the voice service, if it sets these values, wins.
ecosystem.admin_security_voice_invalid: The confidence must be a number from 0 to 1.
ecosystem.admin_security_voice_confirm: Lower the protection of the voice commands? Showing what was said puts personal data in every reply, and a minimum confidence of 0 accepts requests the recognizer was not sure of.
ecosystem.admin_security_voice_heard_warning: Voice replies now repeat what was said.
ecosystem.admin_security_voice_confidence_warning: The confidence check is off: a movement can be started by a request the recognizer was not sure of.
ecosystem.admin_security_mavlink_key_label: File with the 32-byte signing key (empty: no signing)
ecosystem.admin_security_mavlink_unsigned_label: Still accept messages that are not signed (a vehicle that does not sign yet)
ecosystem.admin_security_mavlink_help: Only the path of the key file is saved, never the key; the file must hold 32 bytes or 64 hexadecimal characters. The UAV bridge reads this when it starts.
ecosystem.admin_security_mavlink_confirm: Turn MAVLink signing off, or accept unsigned messages? Without signing, anyone who can reach the link can send commands to the vehicle.
ecosystem.admin_security_mavlink_unsigned_warning: Unsigned MAVLink messages are still accepted: the signing does not protect the link from forged messages.
ecosystem.admin_security_mavlink_off_warning: MAVLink signing is off: the link to the vehicle is not authenticated.
ecosystem.admin_security_mavlink_restart: The UAV bridge applies the change when it starts again.
ecosystem.ai_dashboard_desc: The trend summary, the anomaly check and the fleet view of the AI services, shown inside this app with the same login.
ecosystem.ai_dashboard_other_origin: The dashboard is served from another address than this app, so it cannot use this login inside a frame. Open it on its own and sign in there.
ecosystem.ai_family_desc: The same real ecosystem scan as Services, narrowed to the two families the ecosystem's own manifests self-report as AI. No live telemetry here either - see Config > AI/Hailo to record what's actually installed on this deployment.
ecosystem.ai_family_note: None of these nodes expose an HTTP API of their own yet - every one is a CLI tool/library today. This panel shows manifest/liveness data only, the same as Services, not a richer live AI dashboard that doesn't exist server-side.
ecosystem.ai_family_device_mismatch: {{family}} has live nodes, but its Hailo device is set to None in Config > AI/Hailo - set it to {{device}} to match what's actually running.
ecosystem.logs_no_match: No log lines match this filter.
ecosystem.admin_security_readonly_label: Keep the whole server read-only: nothing is changed from any app, except STOP and the safe-mode disable (off by default)
ecosystem.admin_security_readonly_help: Reading, signing in and STOP always work. Use it to show the cell without any risk of a change; an administrator switches it off here.
ecosystem.admin_security_readonly_confirm: Change the read-only mode of the whole server? While it is on, no app can change anything except STOP and the safe-mode disable.
ecosystem.admin_security_robots_enable_label: Allow a client to enable a robot that is in safe mode (administrators only; off by default)
ecosystem.admin_security_robots_help: Disabling a robot is always possible, like a stop. Without this option a disabled robot can only be brought back from the settings of an administrator.
ecosystem.admin_security_robots_confirm: Allow clients to enable robots that are in safe mode? An administrator will be able to bring a robot back with one click.
ecosystem.admin_security_robots_warning: Administrators can now enable robots from a client.
ecosystem.admin_security_production_label: Set the read-out protection (level 1) when a controller board is flashed in production
ecosystem.admin_security_production_help: Off by default (level 0: nothing is protected). It only records the choice: no flashing tool reads it yet. Level 2 is permanent and is never offered.
ecosystem.admin_security_production_confirm: Turn on read-out protection for production flashes? Level 1 locks the reading of the chip through the debug port; only a full erase of the chip undoes it.
ecosystem.admin_security_connections_label: Keep the address and user agent of each client in the connection history
ecosystem.admin_security_connections_help: Off by default: the history works without them. When on, only administrators are shown them.
ecosystem.admin_security_connections_warning: The server now keeps the address and user agent of every client in the connection history (only administrators see them).
ecosystem.admin_security_connections_confirm: The address and user agent are personal data. Keep them in the connection history?
ecosystem.admin_security_health_label: Let anyone on the network read GET /health without signing in
ecosystem.admin_security_health_help: Off by default: the route then answers as if it did not exist. When on, it shows only a bare health report, for a supervisor or load balancer.
ecosystem.admin_security_health_warning: GET /health now answers without a sign-in (only a bare health report).
ecosystem.admin_security_health_confirm: GET /health will answer without a sign-in. Open it?
ecosystem.admin_security_auth_eddsa: EdDSA (Ed25519, public keys published for other services)
ecosystem.admin_security_auth_accept_hs256_label: Accept HS256 tokens while new tokens are signed with EdDSA
ecosystem.admin_security_auth_help: HS256 by default (shared secret). With EdDSA the server publishes its public keys at /.well-known/jwks.json so another service can verify a token without a secret that could forge one. Keep HS256 accepted until the sessions of before the change have ended.
ecosystem.admin_security_auth_eddsa_warning: New tokens are now signed with EdDSA; the public keys are published at /.well-known/jwks.json.
ecosystem.admin_security_auth_hs256_refused_warnin: HS256 tokens are no longer accepted: sessions opened before the change must sign in again.
ecosystem.admin_security_auth_confirm: HS256 tokens will stop being accepted and the sessions that hold one must sign in again. Continue?
ecosystem.admin_security_auth_rotate_confirm: A new key will sign from now on; the previous one stays valid during the overlap. Rotate?
ecosystem.admin_security_auth_rotate_error: The key could not be rotated.
ecosystem.admin_security_stop_label: Announce a global stop on the MQTT bridge (retained SAFE_STOP)
ecosystem.admin_security_stop_help: Off by default. Needs the MQTT bridge on. The state stays until an administrator releases it.
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_relay_label: Deliver the stop requests of the job dispatcher to the robots (off by default)
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_relay_help: The server reads the stop requests, stops the robot named there and only then acknowledges them. The switch applies on the next start of the server; the robot map applies at once.
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_map_label: Robot map (one per line: dispatcher robot id = robot number in this server)
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_map_help: A robot that is not in the map is never stopped nor acknowledged.
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_map_invalid: The robot map is not valid: write one line per robot as "id = number" (an id of 1 to 64 letters, digits, . _ : - and a number of 0 or more).
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_allow_label: Send a job back to the queue even if the silent robot never confirmed its stop (off by default)
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_timeout_label: Seconds to wait for the confirmed stop (more than 0, at most 86400)
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_timeout_invalid: The wait must be a number greater than 0 and at most 86400.
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_replan_help: The server writes these two values into the configuration file of the dispatcher and asks it to read the file again; if it cannot, the dispatcher reads them when it starts.
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_not_editable: The deployment did not name the configuration file of the dispatcher (HYDRA_UMC_JOB_DISPATCHER_CONFIG): these two options cannot be changed here.
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_confirm: Switch the delivery of stop requests on, or let a job go to another robot without a confirmed stop? Check the robot map first.
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_warning_relay: The delivery of the stop requests is on; it starts working at the next start of the server.
ecosystem.admin_security_jd_warning_replan: A job can now go to another robot even if the silent robot never confirmed its stop.
ecosystem.planning_intro: Read-only views and dry runs. Nothing here moves a robot, queues a job or installs a version.
ecosystem.planning_sim_help: Paste a plan as JSON (steps and, optionally, constraints). The planner checks it step by step on a simulated clock.
ecosystem.planning_sim_invalid_request: That is not a plan: it must be a JSON object with a non-empty list of steps.
ecosystem.planning_sim_accepted: Accepted: the plan breaks none of the declared rules.
ecosystem.planning_sim_rejected: Rejected: the plan breaks the rules listed below.
ecosystem.planning_sim_unchecked: Not shown: part of the plan could not be checked (for example the orientation of the tool). This is not an acceptance.
ecosystem.planning_traj_help: Asks the kinematic replica, through the planner, whether the moves are reachable and within the limits. It never executes anything.
ecosystem.planning_sim_not_executed: Nothing was executed or queued: this is a dry run.
ecosystem.planning_off: This function is switched off in the service.
ecosystem.planning_forbidden: Your account may not use this function.
ecosystem.planning_malformed: The answer is not the one expected, so it is not shown.
ecosystem.planning_http: The service answered with an error.
ecosystem.planning_eta_help: When each job that has not ended is expected to start and end. It assigns nothing.
ecosystem.planning_eta_drain: The queue is expected to be empty in
ecosystem.planning_rul_help: Days until the trend of a list of scores reaches a limit. It is an estimate of a trend, not a guarantee.
ecosystem.planning_rul_points: Points, one per line: seconds, score
ecosystem.planning_rul_invalid: Write at least one point per line as "seconds, score" (at most 1000) and a numeric limit.
ecosystem.planning_rul_insufficient_data: Not enough points for an estimate.
ecosystem.planning_rul_limit_reached: The limit has already been reached.
ecosystem.planning_train_help: Open the file written by `train plan --json` of the updater. It is only shown: nothing is installed from here.
ecosystem.planning_train_invalid: That file is not the output of `train plan --json` (version 1).
ecosystem.planning_dl_help: Read from the data lake itself. They are start-up options of its service, so they are shown here and changed there.
ecosystem.admin_security_exposure_camera_label: Let the camera pictures open without a ticket or a sign-in
ecosystem.admin_security_exposure_ws_label: Accept a token in the WebSocket address (/ws?token=)
ecosystem.admin_security_exposure_log_label: Blank out secrets in the log
ecosystem.admin_security_exposure_voice_label: Require a verified signature on a confirmed spoken request
ecosystem.admin_security_exposure_help: Safe defaults: pictures ask for a ticket, no token in the address, secrets blanked out, signature not required (turn it on once the voice service shares its key). A value fixed by the server environment cannot be changed here.
ecosystem.admin_security_exposure_camera_warning: The camera pictures are now open to the whole network.
ecosystem.admin_security_exposure_ws_warning: A token in the WebSocket address is now accepted; proxies and servers may record it.
ecosystem.admin_security_exposure_log_warning: Secrets are no longer blanked out of the log.
ecosystem.admin_security_exposure_confirm: This lowers the protection of the server (open camera pictures, a token in the address, secrets in the log or no signature on spoken confirmations). Continue?
ecosystem.admin_security_install_camera_label: Hand the password of an IP camera to its process through the environment (not on its command line)
ecosystem.admin_security_install_tls_label: Let a new installation switch TLS on by itself
ecosystem.admin_security_install_help: Safe defaults: both on. The camera option applies the next time a camera process starts; the TLS option is only read at the first start of an installation. A value fixed by the server environment cannot be changed here.
ecosystem.admin_security_install_camera_warning: The password of an IP camera is now on the command line of its process, where other users of the machine can read it.
ecosystem.admin_security_install_tls_warning: A new installation will no longer switch TLS on by itself.
ecosystem.admin_security_install_confirm: This lowers the protection of the server (a camera password on a command line, or no TLS by default in a new installation). Continue?
ecosystem.admin_security_rl_enabled_label: Limit the requests per address (sign-in, renewals, API, code and service routes, global stop)
ecosystem.admin_security_rl_off_warning: The request limits are OFF: nothing stops a loop of requests or a password guesser coming from one address.
ecosystem.admin_security_rl_confirm: This lowers the protection of the server (an address could make any number of requests). Continue?
ecosystem.admin_security_rl_loose_warning: A limit is set very high: it hardly protects the server any more.
ecosystem.admin_security_rl_help: Each number is the most requests one address may make inside its window; the sign-in counts failed attempts only. A number fixed by the environment of the server is locked. A change applies at once and the counters start again.
ecosystem.admin_security_rl_sensitive_max: Requests allowed on code and service routes
ecosystem.admin_security_rl_invalid: Every number must be a whole number inside its range.
ecosystem.admin_bridges_help: Switches of the bridges that move or watch machines. Everything that moves hardware is off by default. The values are saved in the server and, while the gateway to the machine bridges is on, sent to each bridge; a bridge applies them only if its own host allows remote settings, otherwise it keeps what its own environment or file says.
ecosystem.admin_bridges_delivery_on: The gateway to the machine bridges is on: the values are sent to the bridges.
ecosystem.admin_bridges_delivery_off: The gateway to the machine bridges is off: the values are saved but not sent until you switch it on.
ecosystem.admin_bridges_local_label: Read on the bridge host as
ecosystem.admin_bridges_confirm: One of these changes turns on a function that moves hardware or takes a protection away. Continue?
ecosystem.admin_bridges_warning: A bridge switch that moves hardware or lowers a protection was saved.
ecosystem.admin_bridges_signing_title: Signature of the settings sent to the bridges
ecosystem.admin_bridges_signing_help: The settings are signed with one key per bridge, kept in a file on the server (never shown). Copy the key file to the host of the bridge and name it in the bridge's SETTINGS_KEY_FILE variable; a bridge applies a setting only when the signature is valid, current and not repeated.
ecosystem.admin_bridges_signing_key_missing: No key yet (it is made when the settings are first sent)
ecosystem.admin_bridges_signing_key_unusable: Key unusable: nothing is sent to this bridge
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_droids_globalStop: Obey the global stop (refuse jobs while the server announces a stop)
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_droids_cutOnGlobalStop: Cut the Spot session on a global stop
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_uav_missionUploadEnabl: Allow uploading a mission to the autopilot (does not start it)
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_droids_confirmationReq: Require the confirmation of a person, signed by the server, before the droid walks, picks or places
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_droids_returnHomeAlway: Let going home through even if the droid still reports it is busy (never during a fault)
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_uav_envelopeRequired: Require the flight envelope (ceiling and radius) before arming, taking off or going to a point
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_uav_confirmationRequir: Require the confirmation of a person, signed by the server, before arming, taking off or going to a point
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_uav_chainInFlight: Allow a go-to or a hover while the vehicle is already flying (after a successful request)
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_uav_uploadGeofence: Allow loading the radius of the envelope into the autopilot as a geofence
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_amr_publishState: Publish the state of the vehicles
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_amr_publishOpcua: Publish the vehicles to the OPC UA server
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_amr_zoneInterlock: Pause a vehicle whose next node is in an occupied zone
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_amr_zoneUnknown: A zone whose occupancy is unknown counts as
ecosystem.admin_bridges_opt_openpnp_boardCode: Check the board code read from the board
ecosystem.admin_security_ecosystem_health_label: Let operators and administrators read the health of the services (GET /api/ecosystem/health)
ecosystem.admin_security_ecosystem_health_help: Off by default: the route then answers as if it did not exist. When on, it lists each service with its state, the version it reports and the days left of the TLS certificate; only administrators also see ports and units.
ecosystem.admin_security_twin_relay_label: Let the panels follow the live state of the twin through the server (WebSocket /api/twin/ws)
ecosystem.admin_security_twin_relay_help: Off by default: the socket then closes as if the twin were not configured. When on, the server opens the twin's own socket with the sign-in of each person and passes on only what the twin pushes; nothing a panel sends reaches the twin. It also needs the address of the twin on the server.
ecosystem.admin_security_twin_relay_save: Save live state of the twin
ecosystem.admin_security_bridge_gateway_label: Let clients read the state of the machine bridges and let operators send them commands (GET /api/bridges, POST /api/bridges/:name/cmd/:verb)
ecosystem.admin_security_bridge_gateway_help: Off by default: the routes then answer as if they did not exist. When on, the server reads the bridges from the broker and publishes the commands of a short list (stop, pause, resume, status) on their topics; every command is recorded in the audit log. The broker access list should let only the server publish on the command topics.
ecosystem.admin_security_bridge_gateway_save: Save gateway to the machine bridges
ecosystem.admin_security_bridge_gateway_warning: The server now forwards commands from operators to the machine bridges through the broker.
ecosystem.admin_security_trusted_networks_label: Only allow administering the server from the house network and the VPN (outside, only accounts with the second factor can sign in)
ecosystem.admin_security_trusted_networks_help: Off by default. When on, administering the server is refused from addresses outside the networks listed in the configuration file (the private ranges and the VPN), and the policy for the rest is set there too. Check that you are on a trusted network before saving.
ecosystem.admin_security_trusted_networks_warning: From now on the server refuses to be administered from outside the house network and the VPN.
ecosystem.admin_security_rul_label: Let operators use the remaining-useful-life estimate of the AI dashboard (POST /api/ai/anomaly-detector/rul)
ecosystem.admin_security_rul_help: Off by default: only an administrator may then send the request, as before. When on, operators may too; the size and the time of the request are limited, and only this request is opened (every other write to the detector stays for administrators).
ecosystem.admin_security_fram_label: Offer the erase and self-test of the F-RAM of the kinematic brain
ecosystem.admin_security_fram_help: Off by default. Needs the SPI bridge started with --enable-fram-erase and a firmware built for it; an erase also needs the word ERASE typed in the Flasher.
ecosystem.admin_security_fram_confirm: Offer the F-RAM erase? An administrator will be able to write zeros over the whole F-RAM of the kinematic brain from the Flasher.
ecosystem.admin_security_estop_watch_help: Empty or 0: off. Otherwise 500 to 60000. The server reads the physical emergency stop from the SPI bridge at that interval and shows one stop state in the apps. A change applies when the server restarts.
ecosystem.admin_security_estop_watch_invalid: Use 0 (off) or a whole number from 500 to 60000.

auth.title: HYDRA-UMC STUDIO Access
auth.subtitle: Sign in to save changes and receive live updates from other connected clients.
auth.read_only_hint: You can browse without signing in, but changes won't be saved and live updates won't arrive.
auth.keep_signed_in: Keep me signed in on this device
auth.keep_signed_in_hint: Off: the session ends when you close the tab. On: it survives restarting the browser.
auth.totp_needed: This account asks for a second step. Enter your code.

gamepad_config.title: Gamepad Controller
gamepad_config.no_gamepad: No gamepad detected - press a button on it to wake the browser up to it.
gamepad_config.controlling: The gamepad moves {{robot}} - the robot selected in the list

mode.title: Control mode
mode.off_hint: Off. The gamepad moves nothing until you arm it.
mode.armed_hint: Armed. The gamepad moves {{robot}}; STOP is always first.
mode.refuse_no_claim: Reserve {{robot}} for this window first (Robot access > Reserve): the gamepad only moves a robot this window has reserved.
mode.refuse_no_pad: No gamepad detected - press a button on it first.
mode.status_ready: Ready: the gamepad moves the selected robot.
mode.status_blocked: Paused: this window has no reservation of the selected robot. Only STOP and robot selection work.
mode.status_unfocused: Paused: this tab has no focus. Click it, then let go of every stick and button.
mode.status_no_pad: No gamepad: reconnect it, then arm the mode again.
mode.status_stopped: STOP pressed: nothing moves while it is held.
mode.require_claim: Move only a robot this window has reserved

plannerIdentity.title: Semantic planner: who approves a plan
plannerIdentity.desc: The semantic planner releases a plan only when the person who approves it is signed in with a token of this server and is the person named in the approval. This switch relaxes that for a bench without the server. It is on by default; only an administrator can change it, relaxing it asks for a confirmation, and every change is recorded.
plannerIdentity.label: Require a signed-in operator to approve a plan
plannerIdentity.state_on: On: the approval is made by the person who is signed in (default).
plannerIdentity.state_off: Off: the approval is the words of the request (only for a bench).
plannerIdentity.unsupported: This server does not offer the settings of the semantic planner.
plannerIdentity.not_configured: The semantic planner is not set up on this server.
plannerIdentity.forbidden: Only an administrator can read or change this switch.
plannerIdentity.load_error: Could not read the identity switch of the semantic planner.

plannerIdentity.kept_file: The change is kept in the configuration file of the planner across restarts.
plannerIdentity.kept_memory: The change lasts until the planner restarts (it has no configuration file).
plannerIdentity.confirm_title: Relax the identity of the approval?
plannerIdentity.confirm_message: Plans will be released on the words of the request, without the person being signed in. Relax this only on a bench without the server.

opsProposals.title: Node watchdog: proposals waiting for a person
opsProposals.desc: The node watchdog never opens a maintenance incident from a proposal on its own: each one waits here until an administrator approves or rejects it. Approving asks for a confirmation and every decision is recorded under your name.
opsProposals.unsupported: This server does not offer the proposals of the node watchdog.
opsProposals.not_configured: The node watchdog is not configured on this server.
opsProposals.forbidden: Only an administrator can read or decide the proposals.

opsProposals.confirm_message: Approving {{id}} opens it as a maintenance incident. The decision is recorded under your name.

hilBridge.title: HIL bridge: pass verdict of the twin
hilBridge.desc: When this is on, the HIL bridge moves the real robot only for a command whose trajectory the twin passed in simulation (a signed verdict, checked against the exact points). It is off by default; only an administrator can change it, a confirmation is needed in both directions and every change is recorded.
hilBridge.label: Require a pass verdict of the twin before the real robot moves
hilBridge.state_on: On: a real command needs the pass verdict of the twin for its trajectory.
hilBridge.state_off: Off: a real command needs only its risk certificate (the default).
hilBridge.unsupported: This server does not offer the settings of the HIL bridge.
hilBridge.not_configured: The HIL bridge is not configured on this server.
hilBridge.forbidden: Only an administrator can change this switch.
hilBridge.load_error: The switch of the HIL bridge could not be read.
hilBridge.locked: The bridge was started with this switch locked on, so it cannot be turned off from here.
hilBridge.not_ready: The bridge has no twin key or no robot set, so the switch cannot be turned on yet.
hilBridge.no_identity: The bridge does not have the identity key of this server, so the switch cannot be changed from here.
hilBridge.kept_file: The change is kept in the file of the bridge after restarts.
hilBridge.kept_memory: The change lasts until the bridge restarts (it has no file for it).
hilBridge.confirm_on_title: Require the verdict of the twin?
hilBridge.confirm_on_message: From now on the HIL bridge will refuse every real command that does not carry a pass verdict of the twin for its trajectory.
hilBridge.confirm_off_title: Stop requiring the verdict of the twin?
hilBridge.confirm_off_message: The HIL bridge will forward real commands with only their risk certificate, without a pass verdict of the twin for the trajectory.

hubGate.title: Connector hub: callers without identity
hubGate.desc: The decision gate of the connector hub answers only callers that present a signed token of this server. This switch lets a caller on the hub's own machine be answered without a token. It is off by default; only an administrator can change it, turning it on asks for a confirmation, and every change is recorded.
hubGate.label: Answer a caller on the hub's own machine without a token
hubGate.state_on: On: a caller on the hub's machine is answered without identity.
hubGate.state_off: Off: every caller needs a signed token (default).
hubGate.unsupported: This server does not offer the settings of the connector hub gate.
hubGate.not_configured: The decision gate of the connector hub is not set up on this server.
hubGate.forbidden: Only an administrator can read or change this switch.
hubGate.load_error: Could not read the switch of the connector hub gate.
hubGate.loopback_only: The hub does not listen on a loopback address, so the switch cannot be turned on.
hubGate.needs_key: The hub has no key that verifies tokens, so the switch cannot be turned off from here.

hubGate.kept_memory: The change lasts until the hub restarts (the hub has no settings file).
hubGate.confirm_message: Anything that runs on the hub's machine will be able to ask the gate for decisions without a signed token. Turn this on only on a machine you control.

serviceIdentity.title: Identity of the services
serviceIdentity.desc: This server can present a short signed token of its own on every call it makes to the services (status scan, health probes, relays, stop relay). A service whose identity key is on refuses a call that carries none. It is off by default; only an administrator can change it, turning it on asks for a confirmation and every change is recorded.
serviceIdentity.label: Present the identity of this server to the services
serviceIdentity.state_presenting: On: the server is presenting its signed token.
serviceIdentity.state_off: Off: the calls of the server carry no identity (default).
serviceIdentity.state_idle_no_key: On, but nothing can be signed: JWT_SECRET is unset, an example value or too short.
serviceIdentity.locked: Set in the environment of the server (HYDRA_UMC_SERVICE_IDENTITY): remove it there to change it here.
serviceIdentity.own_verifier: Keep a verifier of their own
serviceIdentity.order_1: 1. Turn this switch on first, so that the server presents its token.
serviceIdentity.order_2: 2. Then give the key to the services one by one: as root on the machine, run provisioning/service_identity.py --enable NAME --apply of HYDRA-UMC-OS, restart that unit and check it with --status. This screen never does it.
serviceIdentity.order_3: Turning the key on in a service before the server presents its token makes that service refuse the server.

serviceIdentity.forbidden: Only an administrator can read or change this switch.

serviceIdentity.confirm_title: Turn on the identity of the server?
serviceIdentity.confirm_message: The server will present a signed token on its calls to the services. Turn it on before giving the identity key to any service, and give the keys one service at a time.

ingestSwitches.title: What the server accepts from the services
ingestSwitches.desc: The server can keep the faults of the machines, the outcomes of reproduction scenarios, the status of the developer node, the verdicts of the anomaly detector and a signed record of the voice commands, and can check signed trajectory proposals. Everything is off by default; turning one on asks for a confirmation and every change is recorded. Only an administrator can change it.
ingestSwitches.faultFeed: Faults of the machines (read from the broker)
ingestSwitches.faultFeed_hint: The server reads the fault messages of the broker, read only, and offers them to the clients.
ingestSwitches.scenario_hint: An operator or a service can send the outcome of a run; the server keeps it in a signed, chained record.
ingestSwitches.developerNode_hint: The developer node sends its status with the token of that node; the server keeps the latest one of each node.
ingestSwitches.anomalyFeed: Verdicts of the anomaly detector (read from the broker)
ingestSwitches.anomalyFeed_hint: The server reads the verdicts, read only, and offers the latest one of each series.
ingestSwitches.anomalyVoiceRelay: Tell the voice interface when a verdict turns suspect or anomalous
ingestSwitches.anomalyVoiceRelay_hint: Needs the verdicts above and the voice interface configured on the server.
ingestSwitches.voiceChain: Signed record of the voice commands
ingestSwitches.voiceChain_hint: Every voice turn and confirmation becomes an entry signed by the server and chained to the one before. It holds codes and a hash of the person, never the text.
ingestSwitches.proposalVerify_hint: Lets an operator ask whether a proposal signed with Ed25519 is genuine, current and for that robot. It never moves a robot.
ingestSwitches.keys_label: File with the public keys of the operators
ingestSwitches.keys_hint: A file name inside the data folder of the server, with the public keys that sign proposals. Leave it empty for none.
ingestSwitches.keys_invalid: Use a plain file name: letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.
ingestSwitches.locked: Set in the environment of the server: remove the variable there to change it here.
ingestSwitches.restart: The feeds that read the broker apply on the next start of the server.
ingestSwitches.unsupported: This server does not offer these switches.
ingestSwitches.forbidden: Only an administrator can read or change these switches.
ingestSwitches.load_error: The switches could not be read.
ingestSwitches.confirm_title: Turn on what the server accepts?
ingestSwitches.confirm_message: The server will accept and keep what the chosen services hand to it, or trust other public keys for proposals. Turn on only what you need; every change is recorded.

toolArms.reset_title: Reset the arm state of {{robot}}, tool {{id}}
toolArms.reset_hint: The reset puts back the arm state the tool changer reports. It moves nothing mechanical and works only while the robot is stopped and every tool of it is disarmed.
toolArms.reset_type_label: Type the robot id {{robot}} to confirm
toolArms.reset_done: The arm state was reset. The list shows what the tool changer reports now.
toolArms.reset_off: The reset is switched off on the server. An administrator turns it on in Server Admin.
toolArms.reset_forbidden: Only an administrator can reset the arm state.
toolArms.reset_invalid: The server did not accept the request.
toolArms.reset_mismatch: The text typed is not the robot id, so nothing was reset.
toolArms.reset_unavailable: The tool changer service is not available, so nothing was reset.
toolArms.reset_rejected: The tool changer service rejected the reset.
toolArms.reset_error: The reset could not be sent.
toolArms.refuse_armed: A tool of this robot is armed (or was armed and its report is old). Disarm it first.
toolArms.refuse_moving: The robot is moving. Stop it first.
toolArms.refuse_report_stale: A report of this robot is out of date, so nothing was reset.
toolArms.refuse_tool_not_reported: That tool has not reported its arm state, so nothing was reset.
toolArms.refuse_motion_unknown: It could not be told whether the robot is stopped, so nothing was reset.
toolArms.refuse_no_report: The arm state of the tools could not be read, so nothing was reset.

detectionHef.title: Reports of loaded models (DETECTION-HEF)
detectionHef.desc: Lets the detection service accept the reports of the models it has loaded. Off by default. The server writes the settings file that the service re-reads while it runs.
detectionHef.label: Accept the reports of loaded models
detectionHef.hint: While it is off, the service refuses those reports and forgets the ones it had.
detectionHef.locked: This value is fixed by the configuration of the server and cannot be changed here.
detectionHef.saved: Saved. The service picks the change up within a few seconds.
detectionHef.unsupported: This server does not have this setting.
detectionHef.forbidden: Only an administrator can change this setting.
detectionHef.load_error: The setting could not be read.
detectionHef.confirm_title: Accept the reports of loaded models?
detectionHef.confirm_message: The detection service will accept the reports that tell which models are loaded. Turn this on only if you trust the machines that send them.

liveActivity.title: Live Activity on the lock screen
liveActivity.desc: The card of a robot that an iPhone shows on its lock screen while a job runs, updated by the Apple push service. Off by default.
liveActivity.label: Show the Live Activity of the robots on the lock screen
liveActivity.push_off: Push notifications are off, so the card is not sent even if this is on. Turn them on in the push settings.
liveActivity.level_status_hint: Running, idle, stopped, error or finished. Nothing else. This is the default.
liveActivity.level_progress_hint: The state, the percentage and the step of the job.
liveActivity.level_full_hint: The state, the progress and the panel of the robot: its name, model, tool and the position of its joints.
liveActivity.lock_screen_note: A lock screen can be read by anyone who holds the phone. The server applies this level before anything leaves it: a phone cannot ask for more.
liveActivity.locked: This value is fixed by the configuration of the server and cannot be changed here.
liveActivity.saved: Saved. The cards that follow use the new level.
liveActivity.unsupported: This server does not have the Live Activity.
liveActivity.forbidden: Only an administrator can change this setting.
liveActivity.load_error: The setting could not be read.
liveActivity.confirm_title: Show the robots on the lock screen?
liveActivity.confirm_message_status: Anyone who holds an iPhone with a Live Activity will see the state of the robot on its lock screen.
liveActivity.confirm_message_progress: Anyone who holds an iPhone with a Live Activity will see the state and the progress of the job on its lock screen.
liveActivity.confirm_message_full: Anyone who holds an iPhone with a Live Activity will see the whole panel of the robot on its lock screen: its name, model, tool and the position of its joints.

twinLive.title: Live state of the twin
twinLive.desc: Watch the state the digital twin pushes (the joints of the robot and the vehicles it follows) through this server. It is off by default and only a choice of this browser; this window only reads and nothing it sends reaches the twin.
twinLive.label: Watch the live state of the twin
twinLive.connecting: Connecting to the twin through the server...
twinLive.live: Connected: the server passes on what the twin pushes.
twinLive.denied: The session was refused: sign in again to watch the twin.
twinLive.not_available: The server cannot pass on the twin now: it is not set up, or too many panels are watching.
twinLive.unavailable: The twin cannot be reached; trying again shortly.
twinLive.closed: The connection closed; trying again shortly.
twinLive.state_real: State of the real robot: {{joints}} joints.
